name: HEART of Honolulu Art Street Festival
venue_name: Nuʻuanu Avenue (pedestrian-only closure, King Street to Chaplain Lane)
address: Nuʻuanu Avenue between King Street and Chaplain Lane, Honolulu, HI
schedule_text: Annual one-day Saturday street festival, 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. The 5th annual edition was set for spring 2026. No 2027 date has been announced by the organizer.
description: Free, family-friendly block party in the Chinatown Arts District with art, crafts, live music, food vendors, creative local vendors, performances and interactive arts activities. Nuʻuanu Avenue is closed to cars.
source_label: Organizer page (Downtown Art Center); First Friday Hawaii press release
notes: Organizer identified as Downtown Art Center (nonprofit). The organizer page and a March 2026 First Friday Hawaii press release give Sat May 9, 2026, 11-4. Hawaiʻi Public Radio's calendar listing and an Urban Sketchers Oʻahu post (Mar 31, 2026) give Sat Apr 11, 2026. I could not resolve this conflict, so dates is empty. The vendorsmap 'April 11, 2027 (expected)' looks like last cycle's date carried forward: Apr 11, 2027 is a Sunday. No 2027 date is confirmed by the organizer. The vendor application link was not found on the pages I could read (the 2023 state notice pointed to the organizer page above). Organizer also ran 'From the HEART' Sunset Arts Market, Sept 2025. Instagram and Facebook handles not found.

name: Ho Farms produce pickup (Ewa Beach / Honolulu)
venue_name: Old Fort Weaver Road (Ewa Beach); Republik (Concert and Event Center) (Honolulu)
schedule_text: Per an undated Sierra Club Oʻahu list: pickup Mondays 3-5 pm on Old Fort Weaver Road (Ewa Beach) and Saturdays 1-3 pm at Republik (Concert and Event Center), Honolulu. Not confirmed as current.
description: Online-order produce pickup from Ho Farms, a family farm in Kahuku. The farm has also added fields in Ewa Beach.
source_label: Sierra Club Oʻahu Group, Island Resources (third-party list)
notes: I could not reach a current page on Ho Farms' own site showing these pickups. The same text appears in a Sierra Club blog that the search engine dated to about 2020, and it points to a Local Line ordering page (localline.ca/hofarms). It reads as a pandemic-era online-ordering list. The text does not say whether a subscription or box is offered. The farm's own X account lists hofarms.com as its website, which is the only own-source link I found. Ho Farms produce is also sold through Farm Link Hawaiʻi (a separate seller). Pickup sites are not verified as current, so still_active is null. Do not list until the farm confirms.

name: Kahuku Land Farms Stand
neighborhood: Kahuku (across from Kawela Bay, near Turtle Bay Resort)
schedule_text: A 2017 Star-Advertiser piece said the stands are open daily during daylight hours. Not confirmed as current.
description: A loose collective of roadside fruit stands on Kamehameha Highway (mauka side), across from the Kawela Bay entrance, just past Turtle Bay Resort on the way to Haleʻiwa. The Star-Advertiser says they sell bagged cut fruit, whole fruit, some vegetables and cut coconuts. Most of the produce is grown on farms just behind the stand, on land leased from Turtle Bay Resort.
notes: No own website, social account or organizer found. No street address stated by a usable source; the listed '56-800 Kamehameha Hwy' on an aggregator is Kahuku Farms' address, so it was not used. Honolulu Magazine (about Aug 2026) describes browsing 'neighboring stands' next to Kuilima Farm Stand, which suggests roadside stands are still operating there, but it does not name this collective. A Hawaiʻi Life guide (about Mar 2026) lists 'Kahuku Fruit Stands' open daily 9-5 across from Kawela Bay but ties them to Kahuku Farms, which is at a different address. That conflicts with the independent-stand description. Possible overlap with Kuilima Farm Stand (kuilimafarm.com, 57-146 Kamehameha Hwy, open daily 9-5 per Honolulu Magazine); not merged. Check for duplicates with Chue's Farm Fruit Stand and Kahuku Farms. Duplicate of the next row.

name: Kahuku Land Farms Stand (Kahuku fruit stands)
schedule_text: A 2017 Star-Advertiser piece said open daily during daylight hours. Not confirmed as current.
description: Cluster of roadside fruit stands on the mauka side of Kamehameha Highway across from the Kawela Bay entrance, just past Turtle Bay Resort. Sells cut fruit, whole fruit, some vegetables and coconuts, mostly from farms behind the stands.
notes: Appears to be a duplicate of the previous row. Same findings: no own page or organizer found, and no usable street address. The Hawaii Life blog post on conservation-easement rules (kahuku-land-farms-fruit-stands-new-rules) was not re-opened. Honolulu Magazine (about Aug 2026) mentions neighboring stands beside Kuilima Farm Stand, but the operator and current hours of this collective are unverified. A 9-5 daily schedule in a recent Hawaiʻi Life guide is attributed there to Kahuku Farms, so it was not used. Check for overlap with Kuilima Farm Stand before listing.

name: Kailua Swap Meet
schedule_text: Irregular 'Kailua Mini Swap' garage-sale events on Saturdays, about every few months. 2026 dates found: Feb 21, Aug 1 and Oct 17. Next date not found.
description: Community garage-sale 'mini swap' held with Emmanuel Church Kailua. The Feb 2026 booth page says 30+ stalls for families decluttering, and the church's Facebook page says 32 community-operated booths for the Aug 1 edition. Booths are split between the Emmanuel lot and the adjacent Cole Academy lot.
source_label: Organizer ticketing page (Ticket Tailor); Emmanuel Episcopal Church events page
notes: Dates come from the organizer's Ticket Tailor listings (Feb 21 and Oct 17, 2026) and the church's own events page (Aug 1, 2026). KITV also ran Feb 21. The Facebook post '6/6' (no year shown) is consistent with a Saturday in 2026, but I did not list it as a date. Address 780 Keolu Dr is from the church's own Facebook page. The swap meet's Facebook intro lists 281 Ilihau St, which I did not use. The $25 garage-sale booth fee was stated for Feb 2026 and Mar 2025 listings; shopper admission is not stated. The Oct 17 date has already passed, so check the organizer page for the next edition.

name: Keiki Construction Zone
admission: $35 per person; children age 2 and under free
description: Family event where kids see operational excavators and big machines. It also has horseback riding and livestock encounters, live demonstrations on construction and agriculture, RC cars, a kendama competition, a keiki corner, a farmers market, local vendors, food and live entertainment.
notes: The 2026 venue and organizer are not stated in the source I read. Earlier editions: Ke Alaula Farms, Whitmore Village, Wahiawa (Dec 9, 2023, free, per an organizer page by Max Gainz Inc./Ohana Hui Ventures). The 2025 edition was approved on state Agribusiness Development Corporation land in Whitmore Village, with BZ Services LLC as organizer (Environment Hawaiʻi). I did not confirm that 2026 is at the same site, so side and neighborhood are null. Admission changed from free in 2023 to $35 in 2026. Do not confuse with the monthly Hawaiʻi State Public Library 'Keiki Construction Zone' play program. Vendor application and own page not found.

name: Lei Day at Kapiʻolani Park
schedule_text: Annual, held every May 1 (May Day is Lei Day). The 98th celebration was Friday, May 1, 2026, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. The 2027 date is not announced.
organizer: City and County of Honolulu Department of Parks and Recreation
description: City-run Lei Day celebration with a lei contest, Lei Court investiture, hula halau, live Hawaiian music, lei-making demonstrations, artisan booths and food vendors.
notes: No City Parks and Recreation own page was retrieved, so confidence stays medium. KHON2 and Hoodline say the City and County hosts it, with food vendors and artisan booths. The address is from a third-party events guide (Hawaii Guide). The vendorsmap 'May 1, 2027 (expected)' is only an expected date and the source gives no vendor specifics. No vendor application found. The Waimea Valley May Day event is separate and was not researched.

name: Local Inside CSA (Hawaii Agricultural Foundation, HAF Ag Park Kunia)
venue_name: HAF Ag Park, Kunia (produce source); pickup sites around Oʻahu
schedule_text: Older sources describe produce bags with about a dozen pickup sites across Oʻahu. Current schedule and sites not confirmed.
description: Hawaiʻi Agricultural Foundation program launched in 2015. A HAWAIʻI Magazine article says everything in a Local Inside bag is grown at the HAF Ag Park in Kunia and supports about 25 small farmers who lease land there.
source_label: HAWAIʻI Magazine; GoFarm Hawaii Find A Farmer page
notes: GoFarm Hawaii (a third-party page, search-dated about 2024) says HAF relaunched Local Inside as a platform connecting farmers with the community, previously a CSA program. So the bag and pickup model may no longer run as described. No current page on the organizer's own site was retrieved. The magazine article was dated about 2020-21 by the search engine. The 2020 Star-Advertiser gave localinside.csaware.com. The HAF website is from a directory listing and was not opened. Pickup sites are unverified, so side is null. Not suitable to list as a recurring pickup until HAF confirms.

name: Mahiku Farmers Market
description: Listed as a year-round open-air market of local farmers, growers, artisans and food purveyors (Land Conservation Assistance Network entry, last updated Oct 2019).
source_label: Organizer website (contacts page, dated about 2021 by the search engine); Land Conservation Assistance Network (Oct 2019)
notes: The organizer site exists but the page I could read only gives address and contact (contact named: Sonny Doung; email and phone on page). No current schedule or events found. Weekday hours found on aggregator pages appear to be scraped from map listings, so I did not use them. The 2019 directory entry also listed Hyatt Regency Waikīkī (Tue/Thu) and Mililani (Fri) locations, which are old and unverified. vendorsmap says 'seasonal - contact organizer.' A market-directory page asks whether it is still operating. No evidence it is active in 2026, so still_active is null. Verify with the organizer before publishing.

name: McKinley High School Band & Orchestra Winter Craft & Gift Fair
schedule_text: Annual, held on a Sunday in early December, 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. The 2025 edition was Sun Dec 7. The 2026 date is not confirmed.
organizer: McKinley High School Band & Orchestra (Band Boosters)
description: Band and orchestra fundraiser. Every booth fee goes to the McKinley Band & Orchestra programs. The organizer page has separate food-vendor and general vendor applications and vendor sections: lawn and makai, cafeteria, auditorium parking lot, and library lanai.
source_label: Organizer page (McKinley HS Band & Orchestra, Google Sites); KHON2 (Dec 2024)
notes: The organizer page I could read shows the Dec 7, 2025 edition, not a 2026 one, so confidence stays medium and no 2026 date is listed. Past editions: Dec 3, 2023, Dec 8, 2024 and Dec 7, 2025 (organizer page and event listings), all 9-2. KHON2 (Dec 2024) called it the largest in the fair's 40+ year history and named Cindy Wong as event coordinator, and said KC Waffle Dog would be there. A third-party calendar lists it for December 2026 with the date still to be confirmed. Confirm the 2026 date with the organizer. Shopper admission not stated. Food vendors do appear (the organizer page offers a food vendor application).
